status: Hypotheses for outreach. No organisation has agreed to cooperate. Scores are our judgement from the cited evidence, not commitments.

criteria.problem: How directly the organisation faces the waste-methane, waste-burning or air-data problem CityAir addresses (0–5)
criteria.mandate: Authority or budget to act: municipal company, ministry or agency (0–5)
criteria.relation: Existing link to our work: events, exhibitor or partner records, prior contact (0–5)
criteria.fit: How well CityAir's data, AI assistant and sensor/satellite tools complement what they do (0–5)
criteria.timing: Near-term window, e.g. COP31 in Antalya, 9–20 Nov 2026 (0–5)
criteria.signal: Public commitment or scrutiny that makes action more likely (0–5)

companies.name: İSTAÇ (Istanbul metropolitan waste company)
companies.what: Operates the Silivri and Şile landfills; burns captured landfill gas for energy.
companies.why: Satellite data (Carbon Mapper, analysed by UCLA) rank Silivri as Türkiye's worst super-emitting waste site, averaging 7.4 t methane/hour; Şile emits about 4 t/hour.
companies.offer: Satellite-plus-ground validation of landfill plumes and a public dashboard for residents near the site.

companies.name: Carbon Mapper (satellite methane data)
companies.what: Nonprofit that tracks methane plumes from satellites; its data was used for the Turkish landfill ranking.
companies.why: Already measures the same plumes CityAir wants to validate on the ground; a natural data partner for the methane component.
companies.offer: Joint validation study: their plume observations against CityAir ground sensors near Silivri and Bishkek.

companies.name: Evreka
companies.what: Waste management software (listed as a target in the ISAF Smartex 2026 company map).
companies.why: Waste collection and operations data is the input a landfill-emissions dashboard needs.
companies.offer: Connect waste-flow data with CityAir emissions and air-quality indicators.

companies.name: Netcad
companies.what: GIS and urban data platform (ISAF Smartex 2026 target list).
companies.why: Maps of sites, sources and exposed residents are needed for hotspot analysis.
companies.offer: Hotspot maps and baseline layers for municipal planning.

companies.name: Mavili Elektronik
companies.what: Gas and fire detection (exhibitor at ISAF Smartex 2026).
companies.why: Gas and fire sensors complement landfill-fire and methane monitoring. Listed as an exhibitor at the same fair (ISAF Smartex 2026), so an introduction is easy, but no contact has been made.
companies.offer: Sensor integration and alerting into the CityAir dashboard.

companies.name: Sensgreen
companies.what: Indoor air-quality IoT (ISAF Smartex 2026 target list).
companies.why: Sensor vendor with an existing air-quality product line.
companies.offer: Shared sensor-data standard and calibration support.

companies.name: Food-waste generators (food processors, supermarket chains, catering)
companies.what: Organic waste producers. Zero Waste rules place obligations on chain supermarkets, including waste drop-off points.
companies.why: Organic waste is the main source of landfill methane. No specific company has been identified yet.
companies.offer: Food-waste diversion data and emissions reporting for their own sites. Targets still to be named.

municipalities.name: Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB)
municipalities.why: Owns the İSTAÇ landfills now under satellite scrutiny. Istanbul also hosted the International Clean Air Dialogue (Sept 2026), and the city is listed as a target in our expo map.
municipalities.offer: Landfill-methane monitoring pilot plus a public air-quality dashboard.

municipalities.name: Bishkek city government
municipalities.why: Its dumpsite burns all year, and waste burning is a major PM2.5 source. The Green City Action Plan includes a waste-burning ban. MoveGreen already runs sensors there.
municipalities.offer: Sensor network on the dumpsite fence line and a waste-burning alert system.

ADB: strategy for air pollution in Bishkek

countries.name: Türkiye
countries.why: Host of COP31 (Antalya, 9–20 Nov 2026) and has made waste-sector methane a priority. It has not joined the Global Methane Pledge, which is a credibility gap a platform can help close.
countries.offer: A national landfill-methane transparency pilot tied to the COP31 agenda.

sources.label: Circular Economy Mediterranean: COP31 waste methane

countries.name: Kyrgyz Republic
countries.why: National air-quality and waste-burning plans are in place, and civil society (MoveGreen) is already active. ADB supported 50 national sensors in 2021.
countries.offer: A national waste-burning and sensor-data partnership with civil society.

unscored: Other cities in our 20-city list (Tashkent, Tehran, Cairo, Lagos, Delhi and the rest) and other countries have not been scored yet. They need the same evidence check before ranking.
